newsitem.title: USA: SEMATECH sells Silicon Valley Group stake.
newsitem.headline: SEMATECH sells Silicon Valley Group stake.

text.p: SEMATECH Inc, a not-for-profit corporation based in Austin, Texas, said it has sold its stake in Silicon Valley Group Inc for $14.9 million.
In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, SEMATECH said it sold 701,923 shares of Silicon Valley on November 22 at an average of $21.2526 each.
The shares were sold under SEC rule 144, which allows holders who acquire shares from a company to sell after a holding period.

In a separate filing, SEMATECH said that on Sept. 30, 1994 it bought for $8.024 million a warrant entitling it to buy up to 1.75 million common shares of Silicon Valley. The warrant was exercisable within four years at $13.625 a share.
SEMITECH said it exercised the warrant on April 16, 1996.
It said it bought the warrant to fund Silicon Valley's purchases of capital equipment and other resources.
Silicon Valley is a San Jose, Calif.,-based maker of automated wafer processing equipment for semiconductors.
